statements.markdown: In the strong-shear limit $\sigma/\nu\to\infty$, the wave pressure multiplies the driving coefficient $2\nu$ in the equation for $a_1$ by $\cos^2\varphi\,(1-\varepsilon\tan\varphi)$ (Lemma 2.3). This factor changes sign at $\tan\varphi=1/\varepsilon$, and in the strong-shear limit the amplitude $|\mathbf a|$ reaches its peak after this sign change, as shown in Figure 1. For the perturbed wave with this initial direction, Proposition 2.8 gives a *gain* of at least a fixed multiple of $\exp(\varepsilon^{-1/2})$ on its prescribed interval. The gain is the ratio of the maximum of $|\mathbf a|$ on that interval to its initial value.
